content:
**scalar() stops swallowing a line over one trailing space (#612)**

**Actor:** fix/issue-612-fixreview-a-trailing-space-on-a-key-line (agente)
**Fuente:** issue #612 / plainfiles save on vm

`scalar()`'s `^key:[ \\t]*(.+)$` backtracked, so on a key line with a TRAILING SPACE the `(.+)` captured the space itself. Match succeeded, `.trim()` gave '', `scalar` answered non-null, and `parseEntryList` routed to the INLINE branch — so the block branch never ran and two readable findings read as none. One space was the whole difference. Repair: `(\\S.*)`, one line.

MEASURED before writing: the repair produces EXACTLY ONE failure in 3821, and it is `#452/#478-F2`, the pin that DOCUMENTS the defect. That pin was rewritten in place keeping its id and comment trail, never deleted — deleting a pin because the behaviour it documents changed is how a repo loses the record of why.

THREE THINGS THE TICKET GOT WRONG OR MISSED, all found by measuring:
1. `scalar` has FIVE consumers, not four — `checkpoint-block.mjs`'s `integerField` is the fifth.
2. A real WIDENING the ticket did not flag: `findings: ` with nothing under it goes from unreadable to `[]`. Accepted, because the answer becomes identical to the byte-equivalent clean form which already yields `[]`.
3. `brain-graph/1` has NO EMITTER AT ALL — every graph block in existence is hand-edited, so exposure there is total, not marginal.

WHY `[ \\t]*` STAYS and `\\s*` is a trap: under `/m`, `\\s` eats the newline and captures the following entry inline — rebuilding the bug worse. Dropping the prefix class entirely breaks every normal read.

THE DRIFT GUARD WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED. `yaml-block.drift.test.mjs` got a comment line and zero assertions. Its rows observe only `protocol` and `head_sha`, both of which refuse '' and null identically — so a trailing-space row added there would pass unchanged before AND after the repair, prove nothing, and read as if the repair were covered. That is the rubber-stamp shape. Generalizable: adding a row to a guard that cannot distinguish the two states is worse than adding no row.

VERIFY FOUND TWO UNPINNED BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, both correct, both about to ship untested:
- `rev: ` went from `Number('') === 0` to `null`. `0` was a revision number fabricated from an empty string; null is what the JSDoc always declared.
- An NBSP-LED value was admissible before and is silent after (JS trim strips U+00A0, \\S excludes it). So 'admission unchanged in both directions' was an overclaim — it never widens, and it narrows in exactly this case. Now pinned at the GOVERNANCE layer, not just at scalar's.

Verify also caught the design's mutation table claiming `(.*)` dies 'only on the NBSP row' — measured, 7 rows kill it. Coverage better than credited, causal story false. Corrected in place with the correction left visible, because a design that explains why a suite is safe with the wrong reason teaches the next editor to protect the wrong row.

GIT TRAP HIT, complement of a lesson already recorded: mutating while the real fix is UNCOMMITTED means `git checkout --` reverts past it. And a throwaway `git commit -m 'wip'` is rejected by the commit-msg hook, so a following `reset --soft HEAD~1` lands on the previous REAL commit. Nothing was lost (--soft keeps the index) but the rule is now: commit the real change FIRST, then mutate.

**Where:** brain/scripts/review/lib/yaml-block.mjs, yaml-block.test.mjs (new), parse-verdict.{mjs,test.mjs}, actor-check.test.mjs, decision-block.test.mjs, epic-map.test.mjs, checkpoint-block.test.mjs
